title: The Four Levels as the canon's weighing rule
statement: The canon proposes a rule for weighing any situation at four levels — against infinity, against the Elohim as humanity's creators, against human society, and against the individual self — with love as the constant across all four; this record carries the rule as the canon's explicit ethical method, recorded and citable as proposal, not endorsed as the corpus's own ethics.

includes: The rule as stated: the four reference levels and the love constant, in the canon's ordering
Its position in the normative family: the general method beside the institutional proposals (woh-claim-0032 government; woh-claim-0033 economy)
Its cosmological fit: the infinity level presupposes the frame of woh-claim-0023, which is why the rule reads as the framework's ethics rather than a free-standing maxim
excludes: Endorsement or application by the corpus; artifacts may report the rule, never deploy it as their own adjudicator
Casuistry: no worked cases are recorded, and prose that generates them speaks for itself, not for the canon
Comparison-shopping against ethical theories; philosophical context may be noted, not adjudicated

source_references.locator: The four-levels teaching within the messages' ethical material
The second message's development of the weighing frame

alternatives.statement: Multi-level weighing rules recur across ethical traditions (spheres, standpoints, circles of concern); the canon's version is the genre with the framework's cosmology substituted at the top.
Four reference levels without a priority rule decide nothing; the method names considerations, not a procedure.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0020 or woh-claim-0023 is revised in a way that affects the rule's provenance or frame.
The canon's fuller context changes the levels or the constant.
Public prose begins deploying the rule as adjudicator or generating casuistry, both of which this record excludes.
